Compared to Japan, the uniform price is set high, but since it's over water, it can't be helped, so I'll pass. If three people eat their fill, it costs around 30,000 won per person. Last time, it cost 40,000 won, and looking at the table next to us, it seemed like we were eating a lot.

There are a few menu items (seasoning menu items) that are so salty that it makes you cringe, but the rest are just ok. The pot rice tastes just like it did in Japan, and it seems to be the best for reminiscing about Japan.

Something like a Mega Highball has as much ice as the glass is large, so when you drink it, you don't think it's that much. And since the lemon syrup settles to the bottom, if you don't mix it yourself, you end up drinking only carbonated water...

I don't think there has ever been a complete Japanese brand brought to Korea, but I feel very grateful that Toriki can be enjoyed in Korea as well. However, it is not incredibly delicious, so I understand people who come and are disappointed.

reviews.author: Road Bang
reviews.text:
Long-established Pyongyang dumpling and kalguksu restaurant in Seogyo-dong
‘Unification of North and South Korea’ is also sacred.

As you take a step between Hongdae and Hapjeong, among the trendy stores, a yellow signboard that still retains traces of time catches your eye. This is a long-established kalguksu restaurant in Seogyo-dong that has been consistently loved for its Pyongyang-style dumplings and chicken kalguksu since the unification of North and South Korea.

During lunch time, there is often a long line in front of this small restaurant. People who stop by once become regulars, and regulars come back again and again, holding hands with their acquaintances. Although there is a constant influx of new customers, it is impressive to see regulars supporting this restaurant like roots. As expected from an old restaurant, the kitchen and servers work well together. The food comes out quickly, but nothing comes out in vain. The service is polite yet familiar with familiarity.

The most representative menu item is of course chicken noodle soup. There are two main menus. One is spicy chicken kalguksu with spicy seasoning, and the other is basic chicken kalguksu made with clear and savory broth. The kalguksu topped with spicy chicken salad boasts a spicy yet addictive taste, while the basic chicken kalguksu is made with rich chicken broth that blends exquisitely with the noodles to comfort you to the core. The noodles, which are soft rather than chewy, go particularly well with this broth.

Here, air rice is provided as standard, and this is also something that cannot be overlooked. It's good for eating with non-spicy, well-ripened kimchi, or for a neat finish by wrapping rice in the remaining broth.

Menus that cannot be missed are steamed dumplings and dumpling hotpot. This house’s dumplings have a filling filling, and the skin is moist and thin, making them easy to eat. Dumpling hotpot is a clear and deep soup with plenty of vegetables and dumplings combined. To finish the meal, add fried rice to complete a hearty and satisfying meal.

The inside of the restaurant is small, but has a neat and clean atmosphere and the leisureliness of a long-established restaurant built over time. The friendliness of the staff, how the dishes are organized, and even the speed of service all flow in a certain rhythm.

As the name of the unification of North and South Korea suggests, this place is a place where traditional Pyongyang-style dumplings and Korean-style kalguksu are in harmony, along with the taste of home cooking and everyday warmth that has been cultivated over a long period of time.

If you want a meal that is more precious and does not change in Seogyo-dong, which is full of newness, I recommend North-South Unification. A place that has been in place longer and silently than anyone else. It is already a delicious restaurant in itself.

They even give you a guide telling you to eat little by little as you might sneeze while slurping. They have both regular cola and zero cola, and they also have soju and Hallasan. The rice noodles have a comforting feel to the stomach, and the spicy stew noodles have a dry feel to them, so they don't add much at first bite, but they build up over time. The interior was large and clean, and the interior was luxurious in Chinese style with a bit of a local feel.
We ordered the beef assorted meat.
The places I've been to so far have served half-and-half soup with red and white soup.
Here, there was a little white soup in the red soup. In other places, the Hongtang was as spicy as Shin Ramyun, but the Sacheonli Hotpot had a little less spicy flavor and was spicy enough, so people who are not good at eating spicy food will probably enjoy it. This is not a self-serve restaurant, but the basic vegetables included in the menu are provided, but I don't think I've seen corn noodles separately on the menu. The butju was not too thick and was reasonably tasty. I like Puju and corn noodles a lot, and the Puju here was also delicious. As expected, I like Puju. These days, when I look at Instagram or TikTok, I see videos of people rolling up meat and cooking it, so I tried following it, but it took longer than I thought to cook it, so I only tried it once and spread the meat out and cooked it. Doctors like to eat their food properly, so this method, which does not cook well on the inside, is unlikely to work well. I will visit other hotpot restaurants later and decide, but this place has a 100% repeat visit rate because of the good taste and atmosphere.

reviews.author: See In
reviews.text:
I ate Rajji. Crispy red pepper flakes and sliced ​​and fried lotus roots are topped with fried chicken seasoned with soy sauce and spices such as tzuran and pepper.

The red pepper bugak was sometimes too salty, perhaps because of the soy sauce, but the lotus root was thinly sliced ​​and fried, so it had a potato chip-like texture. The fried chicken is seasoned appropriately without being too salty, and it is fried with peanuts so it is savory and crispy, and the chicken skin in particular has an incredibly crispy texture. And the crispy fried food is flavored with soy sauce, tzuran, and various other spices. To be honest, after eating something like this, I don't think I'll ever be able to eat chicken.

I also ordered white soup, but there are no photos, but various vegetables such as paprika, onion, green onion, bok choy, pepper, shiitake, king oyster, bamboo shoot, and ginger were stir-fried to maximize the flavor, and five-spice soybean paste was added to give the soup as much flavor and richness as possible, making it very tasty. However, this is what I felt at Chinese Bokchun Gold, which I went to a long time ago, but there were too many... Vegetables... they were cut into large pieces like Chinese food, but the amount was not small, so it didn't decrease no matter how much I ate... But if you like that kind of food, I recommend it.

From the quality of the food to the tea served instead of water, the quality is quite good and delicious. Instead, the price range is high. Still, it is a restaurant worth coming and trying at least once. No matter how expensive it is, it was really nice to be able to experience this kind of taste. We ordered a meal, noodles, and two drinks for the two of us, but there was so much left that we even had to take away the rest. If two people are going, it's a good idea to order only noodles or one dish, or take away the extras, so please keep that in mind.

Review of visit to Chungkyung Sikgaek in Hongdae (3-hour waiting experience)

I would like to share the disappointing experience I had while visiting Chungkyung Sikgaek in Hongdae last time. I hope this will be of use to anyone considering a visit.

✅ After waiting for 3 hours, you are informed that you cannot enter.

The wait started at 18:05 and after waiting for a total of 3 hours (until 21:04), I attempted to enter, but encountered an unexpected situation.
Considering that the unlimited refills are available for 2 hours and the closing time is 22:30, I checked the availability and visited with 01:30 (1 hour and 30 minutes) remaining, which is the Maginot line of my standard waiting time. However, the owner expressed his position, saying, “It is difficult to use it because it is closed now.”

✅ Unfriendly reception

In order to understand the exact details, we said, "We have placed a wait and are asking if we can dine within today's closing time." I asked, but I only received the answer that it was impossible.
We asked if we should provide guidance to those waiting in advance, but the only answer we got was, “I was too busy to do that.”

Also, I was embarrassed that during the response process, the boss expressed that he did not understand Korean properly. It was disappointing that even the bare minimum of explanation was not provided properly while the guest was requesting understanding.

✅ Please keep this in mind if you are planning to visit.

✔ Waiting times are likely to be long, and advance notice may be lacking.
✔ Closing time and actual entry time may differ, so please inquire directly.
✔ You may sense unfriendliness in the response attitude.

As I live in the countryside, I visited this restaurant on the recommendation of a friend who said it was a good restaurant, but I was disappointed that I had to return after waiting for 3 hours without even getting a chance to have a proper meal. I think the busier the store, the more systematic operation and customer service it needs. If you are considering visiting, please refer to the above to avoid unnecessary waiting.

reviews.text:
#Changcheon-dong #Hongdae #Hongdae Umjimandu

“Hygienic store, clean Chinese taste: a small business I would highly recommend”

As the name suggests, it is a simple and clean store that sells cute dumplings and Beijing-style black bean noodles.
I visited because I was more interested in black bean noodles than dumplings, and after visiting this restaurant, I really wanted to support it.

#neatness
What you feel when you enter this house is that it is clean and neat.
A middle-aged man and his wife run the business wearing full uniforms.
The store is very clean, to the point where it looks like it's a new store, but it looks like it's been a few years since it opened.

The water purifier and side dish container are clean, but the hygiene concept of this house can be clearly seen in the fact that a chopstick sterilizer is also provided.
Considering that the store has been managed and maintained like this for several years, I have a hunch that this is a house that has maintained its original intention.

#dumplings
When I look at this dumpling, it reminds me of the juicy baked dumplings that are famous in Fukuoka.
They cook dumplings that are a little bigger than your thumb very well, and when you chew them, the juice comes out.
Considering that the taste of the seasoning is a little bit average for a Chinese dumpling restaurant, and considering the fun texture and size of the dumplings, it is quite an interesting dumpling and makes you want to eat it again.

#Jjajangmyeon
They say it's Beijing-style Jjajangmyeon, but they put cucumber and a fried egg on Uni Jjajang.
They say that they originally made it real Beijing-style, but gradually changed it to Korean-style Jjajangmyeon to resolve the complaints of customers who were not used to it.

It is a regular Jjajangmyeon reminiscent of Beijing Jjajang, but the color looks like it was made using Chinese yellow bean paste.
It tastes more like soybean paste than rich chunjang and has a subtle Chinese flavor, making it different from regular jjajangmyeon.
It's not too sweet, has a good soy sauce flavor, and is even fragrant, making it very delicious and unique.

The noodles are commercial noodles, but a little thick.
If it were a little thinner, it would go better with the intestines.

When I asked about the soybean paste, I was told that they used a mixture of chunjang and homemade Chinese soybean paste.
So, when I told them about a place that makes and sells real Cheommyeonjang, they really liked it and said they would definitely try it.
I hope this will be of some help to the owner's sales here.

#source
Two sources are provided.
You have to choose one of the two, but if you speak well, they may give you both.
One is matcha powder and the other is black vinegar sauce.
Both go well with dumplings and also go well with black bean noodles.
If you want to add a more Chinese-like scent and taste, you can enjoy it.

#chayettan
It was a Chinese egg pickled in tea leaves, and they gave me one as a complimentary treat as I was the first guest.
I ate well with a grateful heart.

I like this house from beginning to end.
The taste of the food is not that of a master chef, but rather, the food is clean and concise, making food that can only be eaten in this house.
From management to customer service, the store is calm and clean.

I hope that the two owners will keep their original intentions and the store will prosper even more.

reviews.text:
**Jokbal rice bowl and somtam at Hongdae restaurant Amazing Nong Khai🇹🇭! 🍴👍**

Amazing Nongkhai is a Thai restaurant located in Hongdae, very popular for its exotic atmosphere and diverse menu🌴

### Features
- **Exotic atmosphere**: The Thai flag and foreign staff make you feel like you are in a foreign country 🌟
- **Various menus**: We offer a variety of Thai dishes such as tom yum goong, som tam, and pad thai 🍜
- **Plenty of portions**: Each menu is priced in the low 10,000 won range, so the portions are generous so you can order multiple menu items 🤩 Especially, the lunch menu prices are great.

- **Recommended menu**: Tom Yum Goong, Som Tam, Pad Thai, etc. are very popular! In particular, the broth is evaluated as clean and light 🍲

### Jokbal rice bowl and somtam
I ate Jokbal Rice Bowl and Somtam together, and I was especially impressed by the broth of the Jokbal Rice Bowl! 🤤 This broth adds richness to the soft taste of pig's feet, and goes well with the fresh and spicy taste of somtam! 🌶️

Ssom Tam is Thailand's representative papaya salad, featuring a refreshing and spicy taste! 🥗 Fresh papaya, tomatoes, lemon or lime juice, etc. are used to add freshness, and red pepper paste and gum sauce combine saltiness and sweetness harmoniously! 🌮

If you eat Jokbal Rice Bowl and Somtam together, the taste of the two dishes complement each other and add flavor! 👌 Amazing Nong Khai is a great option to try Thai food in Hongdae! 🌟

reviews.author: inversion
reviews.text:
I had something to eat with a friend, so I visited while looking for a reasonably priced restaurant. Most restaurants serve dishes in the order you order even if you arrive first, but it was nice that here they took orders in the order of visit. Because I was the first customer.. The store is not large, so it seems to fill up with about 4 groups. There is also a waiting machine so you can wait comfortably.

- Salmon Organic Pasta_ 14,500 won
I came to know about this restaurant because of the visual appearance of this pasta, so it was a regular pick. In conclusion, it was just like that. I didn't feel like the salmon salad and spaghetti noodles went well together. Salad with udon noodles!

- Shrimp Rose Pasta_ 16,000 won
There was a lot of scent and taste of shrimp. There were quite a few shrimp on top, and I liked the thick texture of the sauce. Now that I know that I can change it to risotto, I feel a little disappointed. Since the pasta here is all spaghetti noodles, it seems difficult to notice much difference in texture.

- Basil Margherita Pizza_ 14,500 won
It wasn't bad. I didn't know it was thin dough, so it didn't make much of a difference to me, who likes thick dough. Still, the taste itself was worth eating. The mozzarella part was delicious.

There are a lot more menu items that I didn't get to try, but I don't think I'll come back since I wasn't very satisfied with the meal. I felt the portion was a bit small, and the price didn't seem that reasonable, so it's worth going at least once. But the Google Maps rating is so good that I might try a different menu..?!?

reviews.text: It's a place I want to visit again. It's difficult to make authentic carbonara, but I enjoyed it very much. The yolk coating was well done and there was no fishy taste at all due to the use of delicious ground pepper. The only thing I regret is that I wish the bacon had been cooked a little less hard. The shrimp rose pasta had an excellent rose sauce and was full of plump shrimp, so it was plentiful. Considering the cost of living these days and the fact that self-employed people are very frugal with material costs, the food is very good compared to the usual price. I am satisfied. Please note that the noodles are close to al dente. The texture of the noodles was also very good.

reviews.author: Yijin Kim (Jane)
reviews.text:
When you open the door and enter, it becomes a breakfast/deli restaurant that you stopped by during your short trip to Italy.

Prosciutto 13,000 won
Sandwich with ciabatta, Parmesan prosciutto ham, arugula, stracciatella, fig jam, and olive oil. First of all, it looks like there are about two large arugula stems. The soft, creamy taste of the stracciatella moistened the sandwich, and the fig jam had a subtle sweetness and flavor, which relieved the saltiness of the prosciutto ham and added interest to the taste of the stracciatella. First of all, the bread is quite fluffy and the more you chew it, the more savory it becomes, making it very delicious. I always make sandwiches with plenty of fillings, but it was nice to eat a sandwich with less fillings because it was different. I was definitely able to focus on the taste of the bread. I felt that in order to use so few fillings, the bread had to be excellent.

Tuscan soup (small size) 6,500 won
It is said to be a soup made with stir-fried bacon and pork and added potatoes and kale. Is it really this deep and rich in flavor? It's so delicious. The umami taste was subtly good, and it was so bitter and savory that I wanted to try it at home.  Before eating it, I was worried that the taste of the chicken stock would run out or that it would be dry, but I was unfounded. I would have added whipped cream, but I liked it because it wasn't greasy.
